source_text: III. et ita idem Galerius Maximus proconsul in aliam diem Cyprianum sibi reservari praecepit. et eo tempore beatus Cyprianus ductus ad principem et stratorem eiusdem officii Galeri Maximi proconsulis clarissimi viri secessit, et in hospitio eius cum eo in vico qui dicitur Saturni inter Veneream et Salutariam mansit. Illic universus populus fratrum convenit. et cum hoc sanctus Cyprianus comperisset, custodiri puellas praecepit, quoniam omnes in [160 — scan unclear] ante ianuam hospitii principis manserant. Et ita altera die octava decima kalendarum Octobrium mane multa turba convenit ad Sexti secundum praeceptum Galeri Maximi proconsulis. et ita idem Galerius Maximus proconsul eadem die Cyprianum sibi offerri praecepit in atrio Sauciolo sedenti. cumque oblatus fuisset, Galerius Maximus proconsul Cypriano episcopo dixit: Tu es Thascius Cyprianus? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Ego sum. Galerius Maximus proconsul dixit: Tu papam te sacrilegae mentis hominibus praebuisti? Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Ego. Galerius Maximus proconsul dixit: Iusserunt te sacratissimi imperatores caeremoniari. Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Non facio. Galerius Maximus ait: Consule tibi. Cyprianus episcopus respondit: Fac quod tibi praeceptum est. in re tam iusta nulla est consultatio.
thought_title: Overnight custody and refusal before the governor
orientation: Recalled from exile, Cyprian is kept overnight near Sexti and then brought before governor Galerius Maximus, who questions him about his identity and leadership.
pass_a_gloss: And so the same Galerius Maximus as governor ordered Cyprian to be kept back for himself for another day. And at that time blessed Cyprian, after being led to the chief and the stable attendant of the same staff of Galerius Maximus as governor as most distinguished man, withdrew, and he stayed in his lodging with him in the village which is called of Saturn between Venerea and Salutaria. There the whole people of the fellow Christians assembled. And when holy Cyprian had learned this, he ordered the young women to be guarded, because all had stayed before the door of the lodging of the chief in [gap]. And so on the next day, on the eighteenth day before the Kalends of October, in the morning a great crowd assembled at Sexti according to the order of Galerius Maximus as governor. And so the same Galerius Maximus as governor on the same day ordered Cyprian to be presented to himself as he sat in the hall called Sauciolus. And when he had been presented, Galerius Maximus as governor said to Cyprian as bishop: Are you Thascius Cyprian? Cyprian as bishop answered: I am. Galerius Maximus as governor said: Have you presented yourself as pope to men of sacrilegious mind? Cyprian as bishop answered: I have. Galerius Maximus as governor said: The most sacred emperors have ordered you to perform worship rites. Cyprian as bishop said: I do not do it. Galerius Maximus said: Take counsel for yourself. Cyprian as bishop answered: Do what has been ordered to you. In so just a matter there is no deliberation.

pass_b_english: Then Galerius Maximus the governor ordered Cyprian to be kept for another day. Under guard, Cyprian withdrew with the chief and the stable attendant of that same staff to the chief's lodging, and he stayed with him in the village called Saturn, between Venerea and Salutaria. There the whole company of fellow Christians gathered around him. When Cyprian learned of this, he ordered the young girls to be kept under guard, for they had all remained before the door of the chief's lodging.

On the morning of the next day, September 14th, a great crowd gathered at Sexti in obedience to the order of Galerius Maximus the governor. That same day, as he sat in the hall at Sauciolum, Galerius Maximus the governor ordered Cyprian to be brought before him.

When Cyprian was brought in, Galerius Maximus the governor said to Cyprian the bishop, "Are you Thascius Cyprian?" Cyprian the bishop answered, "I am." Galerius Maximus the governor said, "Have you set yourself up as pope over men of a sacrilegious mind?" Cyprian the bishop answered, "I have." Galerius Maximus the governor said, "The most sacred emperors have ordered you to perform worship rites." Cyprian the bishop said, "I will not do it." Galerius Maximus said, "Take counsel for yourself." Cyprian the bishop answered, "Do what you have been ordered to do. In so just a matter there is no deliberation."
